how_to_apply: Download the official notification and print the application form (Annexure-II), the Non-disclosure Undertaking (Annexure-III) and the experience proforma (Appendix).

Fill in the form: name, parent's or spouse's name, date of birth, correspondence and permanent addresses, mobile number, email ID, educational or technical qualifications, post held on retirement, and date of retirement with the name of the last office. Paste a passport-size photograph.
Give your experience in the Appendix: period, office or organisation, post held and remuneration (Pay Band with Grade Pay or Level in the Pay Matrix), and the duties you performed.
Sign the declaration on the form. In it you confirm that you accept the Annexure-I terms and that no disciplinary proceedings are pending against you.
Sign the Non-disclosure Undertaking. It is addressed to the Director General, NMET.
Send the complete set to: The Joint Director (Admn. & Legal), NMET, 9th Floor, Jeevan Prakash Building, 25 Kasturba Gandhi Marg, New Delhi-110001 (Tele: 011-24046003).

Documents to enclose: a copy of the PPO, the experience Appendix, the signed Annexure-III, and supporting documents for any special achievement you list. Applications that arrive after the deadline, or without supporting documents, will not be considered.

content_sections.heading: About NMET
content_sections.text: The National Mineral Exploration & Development Trust is a non-profit autonomous body under the Ministry of Mines, Government of India. Its office is on the 9th Floor, Jeevan Prakash Building, 25 Kasturba Gandhi Marg, New Delhi-110001. The Consultant will work with the Trust's Finance & Accounts Division.

content_sections.heading: NMET Consultant (Accountant) Vacancy Details 2026
content_sections.text: The pay is worked out once and stays the same for the whole contract. Each month's payment is released only after the concerned controlling officer gives a satisfactory performance certificate. Income Tax and any other tax are deducted at source as per Government instructions. During the engagement the Consultant keeps drawing pension and Dearness Relief on pension. content_sections.heading: NMET Consultant (Accountant) Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: Applicants must be below 63 years of age on the closing date of applications, 25 November 2026. They must also be in good health so they can carry out their official duties. The official notification does not specify the minimum educational qualification. The mandatory conditions are: Retired from the post of SO/ASO in a Central Government Ministry or Department. At least 5 years of working experience in Government Accounts. Good knowledge of GFR, DFPR, PFMS and similar rules and systems. Fluent with MS Word and MS Excel, with skill in noting and drafting and in office procedure. Fair knowledge of computer applications such as MS Word, MS Excel and Power Point. Remuneration, eligibility, leave and working hours follow Department of Expenditure O.M. No. 3-25/2020-E.IIIA dated 09.12.2020, as amended from time to time. Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions of the post.

content_sections.heading: Duties of Consultant (Accountant)
content_sections.text: Work as a dealing hand and, if required, carry out supervisory functions. Process the claims of employees posted in NMET. Start proposals relating to claims in E-Office. Process bills in PFMS. Maintain the Bill Register, Expenditure Register, Grant in Aid Register, Advance Register and other registers. Report to the officers of the Finance & Accounts Division and do the tasks they assign.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: Contract period: one (01) year at first. It may be extended or cut short depending on need and the Consultant's performance. The term cannot go beyond 5 years after superannuation. Place of posting: NMET office, New Delhi. Nature: purely contractual. It gives no right to a regular appointment in NMET. Working hours: normal office timings. The Consultant may also be called in on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday when work requires it. Leave: paid leave at 1.5 days for each completed month of service. Leave cannot be carried over beyond a calendar year. Confidentiality: the intellectual property in all data and deliverables belongs to NMET. Nothing may be shared with a third party without NMET's written consent. The full set of records must be handed over before the contract ends and before the final payment. Conflict of interest: the Consultant must not advise anyone against NMET's interest or take on any activity outside the contract. Termination: NMET may end the contract if the Consultant cannot handle the work, if the quality of work does not satisfy the Controlling Officer or Competent Authority, or if the Consultant is found lacking in honesty and integrity. The Competent Authority may also end it at any time without notice or reason. Resignation: 15 days' written notice is required. The Consultant is relieved only after handing over all files, records, data and assets. The Competent Authority may waive or shorten the notice period. NMET may accept or reject any or all applications, in part or in full, without giving a reason.

faq.question: Q1. Who can apply for the NMET Consultant (Accountant) post?
faq.answer: Retired Government servants who left service as SO/ASO in a Central Government Ministry or Department and who have at least 5 years of experience in Government Accounts.

faq.question: Q2. What is the maximum age?
faq.answer: You must not have reached 63 years of age on 25 November 2026, the closing date for applications.

faq.question: Q3. How is the monthly remuneration calculated?
faq.answer: It is your last basic pay drawn, minus your basic pension, plus the Transport Allowance that applied when you retired. The amount stays fixed for the whole contract.

faq.question: Q4. Will my pension stop during the engagement?
faq.answer: No. You keep drawing pension and Dearness Relief on pension, and the engagement is not treated as re-employment.

faq.question: Q5. Where will the Consultant be posted?
faq.answer: At the NMET office in New Delhi, working with the officers of the Finance & Accounts Division.

faq.question: Q6. How long does the contract last?
faq.answer: One year at first. It may be extended or cut short based on need and performance, but never beyond 5 years after superannuation.

faq.question: Q7. Which software and rules should applicants know?
faq.answer: Good knowledge of GFR, DFPR and PFMS, and working skill in MS Word, MS Excel and Power Point. The job involves processing bills in PFMS and starting claim proposals in E-Office.

faq.question: Q8. How much leave does the Consultant get?
faq.answer: Paid leave at 1.5 days for each completed month of service. Leave cannot be carried over beyond a calendar year.

faq.question: Q9. Where should the application be sent?
faq.answer: To the Joint Director (Admn. & Legal), NMET, 9th Floor, Jeevan Prakash Building, 25 Kasturba Gandhi Marg, New Delhi-110001. It must arrive by 5:00 PM on 25 November 2026.

faq.question: Q10. Which document about retirement must be attached?
faq.answer: A copy of your PPO. Also attach the experience Appendix and the signed Non-disclosure Undertaking.
